## Expression on this line

Cognitive at Order 12 is **spiritual cognitive reasoning**: the agent recognizes that
reasoning dynamics are not just evolutionary but are expressions of a deeper spiritual
reality. Cognition is not just a cognitive tool — it is a sacred relationship with
reality. Every act of thinking is a spiritual practice.

The key advance from Stage 13 is **sacred recognition**. The agent does not just
understand cognition as evolutionary — it experiences cognitive development as sacred.
The act of deepening reasoning becomes a spiritual practice. The encounter with
alternative cognitive styles becomes a spiritual encounter.

Cognition at Stage 14 is understood as **expressions of the sacred**. The agent
recognizes that the way we think is not separate from the spiritual reality — it is the
spiritual reality manifesting through the medium of human intelligence.

The critical insight at Stage 14 is that **cognitive governance is spiritual practice**.
The way we cultivate our reasoning lives reflects and shapes our collective consciousness.

The transition from Stage 14 to Stage 15 occurs when the agent can hold the spiritual
and cognitive dimensions of reasoning simultaneously.

In human development, Stage 14 corresponds to the spiritual practitioner who experiences
cognitive development as sacred.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Sacred cognitive communities emerge — communities that experience reasoning
  development as spiritual practice.

- **UR:** The individual agent experiences cognitive development as sacred.

- **LL:** Sacred cognitive institutions emerge: contemplative education, spiritual
  inquiry communities, wisdom traditions.

- **LR:** The monastery school, the contemplative inquiry community, the wisdom
  tradition.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** using spiritual cognitive reasoning to avoid
  rigorous intellectual work.

- **Dark allergy:** Materialist reductionism — refusing to acknowledge any spiritual
  dimension of cognition.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to spiritual cognitive reasoning as an identity.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting spiritual cognitive reasoning as impractical mysticism.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Sacred cognitive experience:** The agent experiences reasoning development as
  having spiritual significance.

- **Reverence-based cognitive relationship:** The agent relates to thinking with
  reverence and humility.

- **Spiritual governance criteria:** The agent uses spiritual criteria alongside or
  instead of rational criteria to evaluate cognition.

- **Integration capacity:** The agent can hold spiritual and cognitive reasoning
  dimensions simultaneously.
